subject: Acme competitive bake-off: next steps & test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lillian Chen <lillian.chen@acmecorp.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Acme competitive bake-off: next steps & test plan

Thanks again for taking the time today, Lillian — great discussion. Below is a short post-call recap, proposed bake-off test plan, owners and timeline so we can align on expectations. Please flag anything missing and confirm the timeline that works for your team.

Call notes (summary):
- Use case: Acme search & summarization pipelines for product docs + customer support transcripts.
- Current evaluation: comparing Redwood inference vs Hyperscaler X and Vendor Y APIs. Key buyer concerns: latency, cost, data controls, and predictable SLOs for peak traffic.

Proposed competitive bake-off (objectives):
- Demonstrate latency and throughput differences across realistic load patterns (burst and steady).
- Show cost per 1K tokens for expected prompt distribution.
- Validate quality parity on your prompt set (accuracy/ROUGE/QA pass rate).
- Prove graceful degradation: model fallbacks and autoscale response under constrained capacity.
- Confirm security/compliance artifacts for procurement (SOC2, data retention, audit logs).

Test plan (high level) + success criteria:
1) Latency & throughput baseline
   - What: p50/p95/p99 latency and max sustained rps at target token length (avg 512, tail 2048).
   - Success: Redwood p95 <= Hyperscaler p95 * 0.85 OR cost per token <= Hyperscaler by 20% while meeting p95 goal.
   - Owner: Aditya Rao (runtime configs & infra)

2) Cost and quantization tradeoffs
   - What: measure token cost across float16, 4-bit quantized variants and CPU fallback.
   - Success: 4-bit profile shows >=30% unit-cost reduction with <=2% drop in quality on prompt set.
   - Owner: Vanessa Ortiz (pricing model / cost calc)

3) Quality and regression tests
   - What: run your prompt set + edge-case prompts, compute pass rates and manual spot checks.
   - Success: pass rate >= baseline or documented tradeoffs.
   - Owner: Dylan Brooks (eval harness)

4) Reliability & routing tests
   - What: simulate partial capacity loss and verify automatic routing/fallback policies and KV cache behavior.
   - Success: <1% error rate during degrade windows and no data leakage observed.
   - Owner: Aditya Rao + Redwood infra team

Timeline (proposed):
- Feb 23: confirm test criteria and share Drive doc + prompt set (attached).
- Feb 26: Redwood runs baseline tests and shares raw metrics.
- Mar 2: review results and iterate on configs.
- Mar 4: joint demo of final bake-off and decision meeting.

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-plan-v1.pdf (test plan + config), acme_prompt_set.csv (your seed prompts). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDeF-acme-bakeoff-plan

Open questions from today:
- Which SLO thresholds does procurement need documented for the contract?
- Are there any specific red-team / PII prompts we should exclude from the eval?

Next steps: please confirm owners & timeline by EOD Mon (Feb 23). If procurement wants SOC2 evidence up front, we'll surface our SOC2 report and audit contact.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Acme competitive bake-off: next steps & test plan

Thanks Marissa — I'll take point on runtime configs and baseline numbers. Quick notes:
- I'll capture p50/p95/p99 with and without KV cache enabled, and include continuous batching profiles.
- For quantization, I'll prepare a 4-bit and a bf16 baseline on our dedicated cluster so we can show unit-cost differences.
- If Acme can confirm target QPS and expected average tokens per request (from the prompt set), I'll tune the batching window accordingly.

I'll aim to upload the first baseline CSV to the Drive folder by Feb 26 morning.

Aditya

Thanks Marissa and Aditya — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from procurement/security before we lock dates:
- Can you confirm where logs and model inputs will be stored during the bake-off? We need to ensure nothing persists beyond the retention window and that audit logs are available.
- Is there a short SOC2 summary and contact to validate compliance artifacts? Procurement would like to review before we approve the test schedule.

Also, for the quality tests: we'll add a private set of PII/edge prompts (won't be shared publicly) — will Redwood be able to run those in an isolated bucket?

If you can share the Drive plan and the HubSpot link, I'll loop in our ML infra lead and schedule the review meeting. Preferred demo window is Mar 3–5.

Best,
Lillian Chen

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Acme competitive bake-off: next steps & test plan

Appreciate the quick feedback, Lillian. A couple quick answers and commitments:
- Logs & data handling: by default bake-off runs will use isolated S3 buckets (or customer-provided buckets) with a 30-day retention; we can shorten retention for the test and provide a signed attestation that data was deleted after the run. We'll also provide audit logs for all API calls.
- Compliance artifacts: attaching our SOC2 executive summary; I'll also share our compliance contact in the Drive folder for procurement to engage directly.
- Isolated PII prompts: yes — we can run those in an isolated VPC/private bucket and prevent any persistence beyond the agreed retention window. Please share a mailbox for the ML infra lead and we'll add them to the Drive + invite to the review meeting.

Timeline tweak: Acme preferred demo window Mar 3–5 works for our team. Proposal: Redwood shares baselines Feb 26, we sync Mar 2 for any follow-ups, and joint demo on Mar 4 at 16:00 ET. If that slot is good for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Confirmed owners: Aditya (runtime & fallback), Vanessa (cost analysis), Dylan (quality/evals), Marissa (project lead & exec communication).

I'll upload the SOC2 summary and Drive invite now.

Thanks — looking forward to the bake-off.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
